full_judgment:
2. The opposite parties Nos. 1 to 11 hereinbefore me instituted Title Suit No. 564 of 1985 for declaration that order passed by the defendant No. 2 the Additional Deputy Commissioner, (Rev.) cancelling the lease of the plaintiffs on 15.8.85 is void, illegal and not binding on the plaintiffs. The case of the plaintiffs-opposite parties was that the land in suit measuring 78.23 acres in plot No. 123 of Mouza Char Wapda was recorded in a block during Diara Survey in the names of the different persons on the basis of their title and possession. The land of plot No. 123 is a reformed land and subsequently recorded in khatian No.1 as khas land of the Government. The Government settled the said land measuring 78.23 to the different persons including the plaintiffs in perpetual lease. They paid the salami after execution and registration of the Kobuliats and the lease-hold lands were recorded in their names and sub-plots Nos. 5, 7, 11, 12, 14, 15, 16, 17, 19 and 20 were created in the names of the lessees. The plaintiffs were in possession on the basis of their respective settlement on payment of salami and rents. But the father of the petitioner collusively and fraudulently got 32.50 acres of land out of 78.23 acres recorded in his name without any title and possession therein. The petitioner thereafter started Miscellaneous Case No. 100 of 1975-76 and obtained shaham by influencing Circle Officer (Rev.) on 23.10.75, 31.10.75 and 10.1.76 in respect of 32.5 acres of land out of the plot No.123 wherein the plaintiffs were not made parties. The plaintiffs instituted a suit for permanent injunction in the Court of Munsif, 1st Court, Sadar, Noakhali against the petitioner and others and also filed an application for temporary injunction restraining the defendants not to proceed with the demarcation of the land on the basis of shaham as granted in the Miscellaneous Case No. 100 of 1975-76. The prayer for injunction was rejected by the learned Munsif loading to Miscellaneous Appeal No. 188 of 1976 which was dismissed by the lower appellate Court on 24.11.1974. Thereafter the petitioner also filed an application on 20.6.85 for cancellation of the lease created in favour of the plaintiffs before Mr. MA Karim, the Additional Deputy Commissioner, Noakhali and S.A. Petition Case No. 20 of 1985-86 was started and the Additional Deputy Commissioner by his order dated 15.8.85 cancelled the lease of the plaintiffs. 

 3. The defendant No. 3, petitioner herein contested the suit by filing written statement. His case was that his father Idris Miah was the owner in possession of 32.50 acres of land on the east side of block 81/123 comprising 78.23 acres of land. But as the said land as wrongly recorded in the name of the Government in khas of Khatian No. 1 his father filed objection case before the Objection Officer on 23.10.68, which was allowed and 32.50 acres of land was recorded in the name of his father by opening a separate diara Khatian No.100 noting 6 annas 13 gondas share in plot No. "423 and on his prayer Miscellaneous Case No. 100 of 1975-76 was started for demarcation of the land and separate shaham for 32.50 acres of land in plot No. s1/123 was allowed by the Circle Officer (Rev.) and he had been possessing the land as a tenant under the Government. The plaintiffs collusively got settlement of the land. As they acquired no title to and possession in the suit land on the basis of the lease the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev.) legally cancelled the lease by his order dated 15.8.85. 

 7. It appears from the judgment of the trial Court that it took into consideration the documentary evidence namely, at A, certified copy of the objection petition filed by M Idris Miah challenging the correctness of Ithatian No. 81/123 in objection case No. 472 of 1968 recording 78.23 acres in the name of the Government; Ext. A(1), certified copy of the order in the said case for opening a separate Khatian in the name of Idris taking out 32.50 acres from Khatian No. 81/123. Ext. A(2), the certified copy of the order dated 28.3.197 of the Settlement Officer dismissing the appeal against the order dated 23.10.1968 passed in the Objection Case No. 472 of 1968. Ext. A(14), order dated 15.8.1985 of the Additional Deputy-Commissioner cancelling the lease of the plaintiffs passed in SA petition Case No. 20 of 1985-86. Ext. B, certified copy of the Khatian recording 32.50 acres of land in the name of Idris Miah in Dag No. 81/123. Eats.A(6), Ext. D the certified copy of the judgment and decree of the Title Suit Flo. 63 of 1976 showing that the suit was dismissed against the petitioner on contest and on appeal by the plaintiffs the decree of the Munsif was affirmed. He also found that Ext. E, Ext. E(1), E(2), the certified copies of the plaint in Title Suit No. 468 of 1986, Title Suit No. 467 of 1980 and in Title Suit No. 466 of 1980 and Ext. A (15), Ext. A(16) and Ext. A(17), the certified copies of the judgments in Title Suit No. 468 of 1980, in Title Suit No. 467 of 1980 and in Title Suit No. 466 of 1980 showing dismissal of the suits instituted by the father of the plaintiff No. 2 Kala Miah and plaintiff Nos. 3 and 9 against the father of the defendant No. 3. The Trial Court also considered Ext. C series the rent receipts showing payment of rent in the name of the plaintiffs father and Ext. F Barga Kabuliats executed by the Bargadars in favour of Idris Miah in respect of 32.50 acres of land. It also considered the evidence of both the PWs and DWs. 

 8. The learned Assistant Judge further found that Shamsul Hoq opposite party No. 5 and Bazlul Karim, husband of the opposite party No. 11, were Government servant and they fraudulently obtained the settlement in their favour of the land measuring 2.50 acres in violation to the Government Circulars. The Assistant Judge further found on the basis report of the Surveyor that the land of the defendant No. 3 situates on the eastern side of Plot No. 81/123 and he held that Khatian 100 was correctly opened in the name of the defendant No. 3 on the basis of the order dated 23.10.68 of the Objection Officer and the order dated 20.8.1974 of the Settlement Officer. Upon such findings the learned Assistant Judge held that the kabuliats executed by the plaintiffs in favour of the Government are paper transaction in as much as the Government having had admitted the title of the defendant in the disputed land can not subsequently settle the same with the plaintiffs. But this finding of the trial Court has been reversed by the lower appellate Court with cogent reasons on consideration of the evidence on record. 

 9. The lower Appellate Court on the basis of the report submitted on 9.2.1980 by the Commissioner appointed in Title Suit No. 63 of 1976 found that the land of DS Plot Nos. 22, 23, 24 of Khatian No. 162, DS Plot Nos. 93, 94, 95, 94/1 of Khatian No. 539, Plots Nos. 50, 51, 70 of Khatian No. 537, Plots Nos. 71, 72, 91, 96 of Khatian No. 538 and DS Plots Nos. 49, 52 and 69 of Khatian No. 536 of No. 258 Mouza Char Jubilee which was claimed by the father of the defendant No. 3 does not correspond to the land of the Diara Block Plot No. 81/123 and accordingly held that the order passed on 23.10.1968, Ext. A(a), in objection case No. 471 of 1968 was without any basis as the land of Idris Miah was not identical with the suit land. The learned District Judge also observed on the basis of Ext. A that while claiming the title and possession of the disputed land Idris Miah did not furnish the quantity of the land covered by his alleged pattan nor he disclosed the date when he took the settlement of the land appertaining to DS Khatian Nos. 162, 536, 537, 538 and 539 as his raiyati land which he alleged was incorporated in Block Plot No. 81/123 or Mouza Char Vvrapda. He also found that from the certified copy of the order dated 23.10.68, Ext. A(1) passed by the Objection Officer there was nothing to show that Idris Miah ever produced any paper in support of his claim of pattan from the Ex-land lords but Khatian No. 100 was opened in the name of Idris Miah for 32.50 acres of land showing 6 annas 13 gonads share in Plot No, 8'623. On consideration of Ext. 7, the lower appellate Court also found that. Diara Khatian No. 100 opened in the name of Idris Miah was illegal, collusive and without any basis and the Government claimed the entire 78.23 acres recorded in diara block Plot No. 81/123 as the Government khas land out of which the Government settled the land in dispute in perpetual lease to the different persons including the plaintiffs obtaining kabuliats from them and the claim of Abdul Kader Chowdhury, defendant No. 3 is not identical with the land in suit appertaining to Plot No. 81/123. The learned Judge on consideration of Ext. A found that Idris Miah did not furnish any particular about his pattani land in the objection case and in the written objection Ext. 7(A) in Title Suit No. 63 of 1976, the defendant No. 3 for the first time disclosed particulars of land of their settlement. It appears on the basis of an application filed by the plaintiffs, the learned Munsif appointed a survey knowing Advocate Commissioner for the purpose of investigation who submitted his report on 9.2.80 but the learned Munsif without accepting the report dismissed the suit. The learned District Judge on perusal of the report found that the Advocate Commissioner on relayment found that the land of DS Plot Nos. 22, 23, 24, 93, 94, 95, 94/1, 50, 51, 70, 71, 91, 69, 49 of No. 258 of Mouza Char Jabilee does not attract the land of Diara Block Plot No. 81/123. On consideration of this material evidence the learned District Judge held that the objection Case No. 472 of 1968 was allowed without any basis and it did not create any legal right in favour of Idris Miah. The learned District Judge further found that while on the basis of the lease the plaintiffs were in possession Abdul Kader Chowdhury filed the Miscellaneous Case. 100/75-76 for allotment of separate shaham from Block Plot No. 81/123 and got an order made in his favour and that order necessitated in institute of the Title Suit No. 63 of 1970 on 21.1.76 against Abdul Kader Chowdhury and others for permanent injunction followed an application for temporary injunction not to proceed with the demarcation of the land in pursuant to shaham allotted to the defendant No. 3 Abdul Kader Chowdhury in the aforesaid Miscellaneous Case No. 100 of 1975-76. Against the said order the plaintiffs preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 188 of 1976 and prayed for temporary injunction which was rejected by Mr. Amiya Bhushan Podder, District Judge by his order dated 30.11.76 and the appeal was subsequently dismissed by another Subordinate Judge on 24.11.74. The learned District Judge further noticed that due,to observation made in Title Suit No. 63 of 1976 several suits were filed which however were dismissed on different dates and against the decree of dismissal of Title Suit No. 465 of 1980 Title Appeal No. 11 of 1989 was preferred and during pendency of that appeal in respect of 27.50 acres of land, the defendant No. 3 petitioner herein started SA Petition Case No. 20 of 1985-86 and obtained an order 15.8.85 from the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev.), Noakhali cancelling the lease made in favour of the plaintiff. On consideration of the aforesaid evidence the learned District Judge held that the order dated 15.8.85 of defendant No. 2 was illegal.
